intro: A bowl of bubur lambuk is about 320 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the rice, followed by the oil for frying the spices and the santan (if used).

variants.name: Beef bubur lambuk with thick santan
Big bowl from the masjid (full container)
With cakwe or fried kuih on the side

diet: Yes, and bubur lambuk is actually one of the lighter choices. It has a lot of water, so you feel full quickly for moderate calories. But it's a bit low in protein, so hunger can come back fast. Watch the bowl size and what you eat with it.
tips: Take one normal bowl and save the rest of the masjid bubur for tomorrow.
Add a boiled egg or a piece of chicken on the side for more protein.
Go easy on fried shallots and skip the fried kuih on the side.

swap.name: Plain chicken porridge + boiled egg
swap.why: No santan and less oil, but more protein thanks to the egg.

faq.q: Is bubur lambuk good for buka puasa?
faq.a: Yes. It's gentle on an empty stomach and gives slow energy. Drink water first, then eat the bubur.

faq.q: How long can I keep bubur lambuk?
faq.a: About 2 days in the fridge, in a covered container. Reheat until boiling and add a little water, as the bubur will thicken.

faq.q: What's the difference between bubur lambuk and plain rice porridge?
faq.a: Bubur lambuk is cooked with spices, meat and vegetables, sometimes with santan. Plain rice porridge is simpler and lighter.
